images.caption: Figure 1:Overview ofCaPtain.Top:inference, one episode inCaPtain-Harness: at each request the policy writes a Python cell against a low-level API and receives text receipts and new images, for up to 60 requests.Bottom:training and test: SFT on synthetic agent trajectories, then RL in which a simulator critic turns privileged physical state into per-request credit; the critic is removed at test time.

Figure 4:Real-robot episodes.Two tasks with new objects and layouts; ten frames per episode, with time stamps. (b) requires reasoning about the instruction: the agent must infer that the cube with the color of the sky is the light-blue one and that the container that is not round is the rectangular tray.
Figure 5:The twin simulation used to adapt the policy to the XR1 arm (left) and the real scene at test time (right).

Figure 6:Design ofCaPtain-Harness.The policy writes Python into a persistent session ① that exposes only low-level primitives ②; motions are executed with IK and guarded contact ③, every call returns a receipt ④, a completion gate checks the agent’s own measurements ⑤, and environment-specific backends sit below the API ⑥.
Receipt values are illustrative.
